name: Inflatable Robotic Truss
role: Compliant Mechanisms & Robotics - Graduate Research Assistant
award: Presented at NASA Big Idea Challenge Forum and LSIC, Las Vegas
description: As part of my masters degree, I redesigned the automated roller mechanism for an inflatable robotic truss, achieving dramatic weight and cost reductions while doubling structural strength. Engineered a multi-stage gear train using off-the-shelf components to improve torque and reliability.
highlights: 31% weight reduction, 51% cost savings, 2× structural strength
Constructed 21 roller units with custom vise fixtures for precision machining
Presented to NASA planetary scientists at 2024 Big Idea Challenge Forum & Lunar Surface Innovation Consortium (LSIC) in Las Vegas

name: BYU Mars Rover
award: 3rd Place — 2024 International University Rover Challenge · 102 Universities
description: Led two teams of six engineers to design and integrate the rover's wheel, serial manipulator, elevator, and antenna subsystems. Developed testing procedures that significantly reduced backlash and improved precision in the manipulator arm.
highlights: 3rd place overall among 102 universities worldwide
Highest score among all teams in Science and Equipment Servicing, two of four competition tasks

name: Pneumatic Continuum Serial Manipulators
description: Engineered and assembled four pneumatic continuum serial manipulators for soft robotics modeling research. Performed tensile testing and stress–strain analysis to select spine materials across 12 continuum joints.
highlights: Performed tensile testing and stress–strain analysis to select the optimal material and construction for the spine of 12 continuum joints
Assembled and integrated pneumatic joints for experimental validation of 4 continuum arms

name: Autonomous Ball Scoring Competition Robot
award: Highest Score — 2022 Mechatronics Design Competition · 20 Teams
description: Designed and built an autonomous mechatronic robot to collect, sort, and score black and white ping-pong balls into dynamically changing targets — achieving 28/29 shots and the highest competition score among 20 teams.
highlights: 28/29 successful shots; highest score among 20 competing teams
Flywheel shooting system with color-based servo-actuated ball selection
PIC24 microcontroller in C: line following, sensor fusion, autonomous navigation
Laser-cut & heat-formed acrylic electronics enclosure

images.title: Final Design of the Robot
images.description: Our robot features a funnel and gravity fed system to collect, store, and feed the balls. A color sensor is used to determine the color of the ball and a servo-actuated gate directs the ball to the flywheel which propels it along a precisely angled ramp to shoot it into the appropriate goals. Additionally, the robot uses line following for navigation.

images.title: Our Robot Performing In The Competition
images.description: The robot was required to collect and store white and black ping pong balls by disrupting the green laser and shoot them into goals that randomly changed which ball color they would accept throughout the match. Our team scored 28 out of 29 balls, achieving the highest score among 20 teams.

images.title: Storing and Collection System
images.description: This shows the funnel and gravity fed system I designed to collect exaclty 4 balls as per competition requirements. Any additional balls would fall right out of the system to prevent loss of points.

images.title: Protective Case
images.description: The enclosure I designed and manufactured using laser cutting and heat forming to protect the electronics and provide wire management. This is one of the very few robots that implemented such a protection feature.

images.title: Launching System
images.description: This is the servo-actuated gate that I created to feed the balls into the flywheel.

images.title: Robot Render
images.description: A frontal view of the complete robot CAD model.

name: Handhold — Surgical Clip for Hand Surgery
description: A surgical clip for finger stabilization and incision retraction that interfaces with the "Lead Hand" surgical positioning system. Designed to reduce operating time and required personnel during hand surgery.
highlights: Used in a live hand surgery procedure at Spanish Fork Hospital
30+ prototypes refined through direct feedback from five hand surgeons
Met autoclave sterilization requirements for clinical use
Evaluated single-use vs. reusable variants based on market demand and margins
Finalist among 38 teams at the 2026 BYU Student Innovator of the Year competition

images.title: Handhold Surgery
images.description: This shows the Handhold clip securing two fingers during a trial live surgery procedure at the Spanish Fork Hospital. The clip successfully fixtured the two fingers during the entire procedure, preventing movement and refixturing that would require precious time and effort from the surgical team. This trial shows the clinical viability of the Handhold clip and provided invaluable feedback for further design iterations.

images.title: SIOY Competition Presentation
images.description: The Handhold team presenting at the 2026 BYU Student Innovator of the Year competition where we were finalists among 38 teams. This was a great opportunity to share our work with the BYU community and receive feedback from judges and attendees.

images.title: Handhold Design and Functionality
images.description: This graphic I created illustrates the design and functionality of the Handhold clip. The clip is designed to be attached to the "Lead Hand" using a precision friction fit. An elastic band is then used to secure the finghers and standard surgical retractors can be attached to the clip to provide incision retraction.

images.title: Handhold Clip
images.description: A simple plastic prototype of the Handhold clip. Although this prototype is 3D printed, the final design will be injection molded out of Polypropylene to meet the strength, flexibility, and sterilization requirements for clinical use.

name: Camping Shovel
description: Designed and manufactured a lightweight camping shovel through a structured engineering design process involving market research, material selection, structural analysis, and fabrication. The blade was heat treated through quenching and tempering to achieve a hardness of 51.3 HRC while maintaining durability during digging and prying tasks. The final shovel was approximately 30% lighter than the average commercially available camping shovel.
highlights: Performed engineering analysis and material selection using bending, hardness, and weight calculations
Manufactured the shovel using sheet metal rolling, end milling, and heat treatment processes such as quenching and tempering
Achieved a final blade hardness of 51.3 HRC with a shovel weight 30% lower than comparable commercial products

images.title: Shovel Completed
images.description: Final manufactured camping shovel designed for lightweight portability and durability during outdoor use. The blade is made of quenched and tempered steel to achieve a high hardness and yield strnegth. The handle is made of aluminum to reduce weight while maintaining sufficient strength for digging and prying tasks.

name: Personalized Ski Design Optimization Tool
description: A Python optimization framework that generates custom, lightweight ski geometries from user-specific inputs (height, weight, riding style). Integrated a live Onshape CAD model via API to update geometry and retrieve mass at each iteration.
highlights: ~30% mass reduction vs. commercial skis while maintaining performance constraints
Live Onshape CAD integration via API — geometry updates at each optimizer step
SLSQP constrained optimization over length, waist width, camber, thickness

images.title: Variable Studio
images.description: The variable studio used to define the ski geometry and update it at each iteration of the optimization process. The variable studio allows the optimizer to modify the ski geometry based on the design variables and constraints defined in the optimization framework.

images.title: Ski Geometry and Design Variables

images.title: Python Program
images.description: An overview of the Python program I developed for this optimization project. First, user inputs are defined, then the program creates bounds for all paramters. Then, an initial guess is generated and the optimization process is iteratively performed.

images.title: Optimization Framework
images.description: An overview of the optimization framework showing how the design variables, Onshape API, constraints, and objective function are integrated together to perform the optimization process.

images.title: Onshape API Integration
images.description: Integration of the Onshape CAD API for live geometry updates during optimization.

images.title: API Gif

images.title: Optimization Results for Powder Skis
images.description: This is one of the optimization results showing the optimized ski geometry for a powder ski design. The optimized design achieves a significant mass reduction with an increase in turn radius (less maneuverability).

images.title: Optimization Results for Carving Skis
images.description: This is another optimization result showing the optimized ski geometry for a carving ski design. The optimized design achieves similar mass and performance characteristics to skis on the market, validating the optimization approach.

name: Goal Convergence & Obstacle Avoidance — Kuka LBR Arm
description: Built a complete Python kinematics library for a 7-DOF Kuka LBR arm including DH parameterization, forward/inverse kinematics, Jacobian computation, and a potential field obstacle avoidance algorithm for both static and dynamic obstacles.
highlights: Implemented Denavit–Hartenberg parameterization for 7-DOF arm
Potential field methods applied at joints and along links for obstacle avoidance
Generated linear, circular, and spiral dynamic obstacle trajectories for testing

name: Robotic Arm Project
description: Designed and built a 6 degree-of-freedom robotic arm that can grasp and manipulate objects. The arm was designed in Fusion 360 and the parts were 3D printed and assembled with servo motors for actuation. The arm was controlled using an Arduino microcontroller and custom circuitry that used PWM and potentiometers to interface with the servos.
highlights: Designed the arm with 6 degrees of freedom to allow for a wide range of motion and dexterity
Built custom circuitry to control the servo motors using an Arduino microcontroller
Implemented a control scheme using potentiometers to adjust the position of each joint and allow for manual control of the arm

description: Designed and built a level 1 solid-fuel rocket by combining off-the-shelf components and custom parts manufactured using laser-cutting. Manufactured the fins using a laser cutter and assembled the rocket
Successfully launched the rocket and deployed the parachute for a safe landing
